intro.name: The beginning
intro.text: Following a suspicious discovery, (Accused) is brought before a council of elders. The object rests on a woven mat. Some accuse (accused.him/her) of spying; others defend (accused.his/her) curiosity.

a1.text: Innocent: Evidence clears (Accused), who is publicly vindicated.

a2.text: The Hidden Visitor: Strange footprints and materials suggest someone else has recently visited the island.

a3.text: The False Confession: Frightened, (Accused) admits to something untrue; another witness eventually exposes the mistake.

a4.text: The Unexpected Spy: Another villager planted the object to discredit (Accused).

b1.text: The Wrongful Prisoner: (Accused) is innocent. Later revelations bring shame upon the council and demands for restitution.

text_only.reason: rule 7: a guarded shelter and the council's restitution are told only

b2.text: The Prisoner's Discovery: In confinement, (Accused) recalls a crucial clue about the object's arrival.

b3.text: The Village Divided: Supporters demand release while fearful villagers demand continued confinement.

b4.text: The Escape: (Accused) flees into the forest; the village cannot decide whether this proves guilt or desperation.

c1.text: The Vindicated Explorer: The accusation collapses; (Accused) receives public thanks for the discovery.

text_only.reason: narrative: the accusation collapses; no structure is involved

c2.text: The Unanswered Suspicion: (Accused) is freed, but rumors persist.

c3.text: The Courageous Elder: An elder argues that fear must not become an excuse for cruelty, winning grudging respect.

c4.text: The Genuine Conspiracy: The relic was planted deliberately, although (Accused) may still be innocent.
